guitar.evidence: Extremely well documented: B.B. King's guitars were all nicknamed "Lucille", and his standard instrument for decades was the Gibson ES-355 (later a signature Gibson Lucille model based on the ES-355).

tone.target: warm B.B. King lead clean-breakup with tight midrange, no wah
tone.profile: warm B.B. King lead clean-breakup with tight midrange, no wah
tone.summary: A clean, mid-focused chain using a low-wattage US amp model (Silver Twin) paired with a vintage 2x12 cabinet to emulate the classic B.B. King sound.

rig.name: Bb King - Three O'Clock Blues EDITED - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Slightly boost the signal and emphasize warm midrange frequencies.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used here to gently shape the tone rather than provide heavy gain, mimicking a subtle pre-amp EQ lift.

blocks.purpose: Provide light tube breakup and warmth without sounding like modern distortion.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is chosen for its classic, non-agressive overdrive character, fitting the 'light tube breakup' requirement.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the low-wattage, clean Fender sound required for B.B. King's style.
Simulate the sound of a small, vintage American cabinet (1x12 clue) with a dry close mic feel.
blocks.gap: The US 2x12 is the closest available model to simulate a single-cabinet setup and classic Fender voicing.

blocks.purpose: Further enhance the warm midrange and tighten the overall tone.
Provide a subtle vibrato effect for vocal-like sustain without sounding artificial.
blocks.gap: Chorus is used to achieve the 'subtle vibrato' requirement, as dedicated vibrato/tremolo settings are not available in the compact catalog. Settings are kept minimal.

blocks.purpose: Add a touch of natural room ambience to enhance sustain and depth.
blocks.gap: The Room module is used sparingly to provide subtle air and dimension, fulfilling the 'vocal-like sustain' requirement without heavy reverb.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and midrange focus for authentic B.B. King tone.

proposals.reason: Better captures the small, vintage single-cab sound and tight mids.
